claims.value: <ID>_<wt|mut>_pulldown_light_lysate_membrane / _heavy_lysate_membrane and blank_spot_B<n>_light_lysate_membrane / _heavy_lysate_membrane (one source per physical spot; each source name occurs in exactly one row; ID verbatim from the PRIDE table, e.g. P11166_P485L, SOS1_cntrl)
claims.evidence: Each spot on each of the two membranes (one incubated with light, one with heavy lysate) is one physical pull-down, so the wt spot of a pair on the light-lysate membrane (light channel of the Fw run) and the wt spot on the heavy-lysate membrane (heavy channel of the Rev run) are different sources (review round 1 finding 1); PRIDE/preprint: "Single spots were punched out ... and SILAC pairs were placed together"; IDs are UniProt accession + mutation as listed by the submitters. Blank runs B1-B3 are labelled "B blank" in the PRIDE table.

claims.value: "<ID> wild-type peptide" / "<ID> mutant peptide"; "no peptide (blank membrane spot)" for B1-B3
claims.evidence: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol: "Experimental setup: Fw: Light- Wt, Heavy-Mut Rev: Light-Mut, Heavy-Wt" with table "Fw Rev ID 1 2 SOS1_cntrl 3 4 Q9NRG9_Q15K ... 263 264 WIP_cntrl B blank". Run number = PepArray2_<NNN> file number = MaxQuant experiment E<NNN> (summary.txt). So run 2k-1 (Fw): light channel = wild-type peptide pull-down, heavy = mutant; run 2k (Rev): light = mutant, heavy = wild-type. Preprint: "Wild-type peptide spots from the heavy pull-down are combined with spots from the light pull-down that correspond to the mutant forms of the same peptide, and vice versa." Cross-check against deposited ratios (orientation.txt): clathrin (CLTC/CLTA/CLTB) H/L 8-50 in Fw and 0.007-0.05 in Rev for P11166_P485L (GLUT1), Q14643_P1059L (ITPR1), O95180_P648L (CACNA1H), matching the paper's mutation-induced clathrin gain; GRB2/NCK1 H/L 0.05/0.11 (Fw) and 37.7/14.3 (Rev) for SOS1_cntrl, matching SH3 binders preferring wild-type SOS1 (preprint Fig. 1C). Control IDs have wt and mut forms: proteinGroups lists SOS1_cntrl_wt/_mut and WIP_cntrl_wt/_mut entries from the peptide fasta; preprint Fig. 1C legend "wild-type and mutant SOS1 peptide".
Same Fw/Rev channel map as characteristics[bait]; custom characteristics column (spec Extending Templates) so the wild-type vs mutant axis is filterable separately from the peptide pair.

claims.value: 1 = pull-down from the light-SILAC-lysate membrane, 2 = from the heavy-SILAC-lysate membrane, within each factor value[bait] group
claims.evidence: The number denotes the lysate/membrane, not a per-group count: 1 = light-SILAC lysate culture and its membrane, 2 = heavy-SILAC lysate culture and its membrane; it is therefore always 1 on SILAC light rows and 2 on SILAC heavy rows. Consequences: Q9UQN3_T104N wild-type has only replicate 2 and its mutant only replicate 1 (its Fw run 039_new is not deposited); the three blank spots per membrane (B1-B3) share replicate 1 (light) or 2 (heavy) because they are spots on the same membrane incubated with the same lysate, distinguished by source name. Protocol: "Two of those peptide filters ... The entire peptide libraries were incubated with 15 ml of light or heavy SILAC labeled cell lysate"; preprint: "two replicates of a pull-down with a specific peptide sequence", "incubating the two replicates of the membrane with cell lysates that have been differentially SILAC labeled". Each bait therefore has two independent pull-downs (separate membrane, separately labelled culture). Numbering is by membrane/lysate so it is consistent across groups; for Q9UQN3_T104N only one replicate per variant is deposited (see limitations).

claims.evidence: PRIDE table labels runs B1-B3 "B blank" (no peptide spot). PRIDE:0001016 blank (OLS definition: "A sample or analytical run lacking the intended analyte and used to characterize background or contamination associated with an experimental workflow") - here the intended analyte (the bait peptide) is absent and the run captures background binding of lysate proteins to the cellulose membrane (L and H lysate proteins present in proteinGroups). PRIDE:0001013 study sample for all peptide pull-downs. Upstream base 1.1.0 (via ms-proteomics 1.2.0) recommends the column with default study sample, children of PRIDE:0000895.
human template recommends the column; Cellosaurus CVCL_0019 gives no donor identifier for the SH-SY5Y (SK-N-SH) donor, so the reserved word is used.

limitations: Runs PepArray2_037_new, 038_new and 039_new appear in the deposited MaxQuant summary.txt (experiments E037-E039) but their .raw files are not in the PRIDE file list, so they cannot be annotated. Per the PRIDE table these are Fw+Rev of Q8WYQ3_P34S (pair absent from the SDRF entirely) and the Fw run of Q9UQN3_T104N (only its Rev run 040 is deposited, so Q9UQN3_T104N wild-type has only replicate 2 and mutant only replicate 1).

The Cell paper (doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.08.019) is not open access in PMC and the Unpaywall publisher PDF returned HTTP 403 (not bypassed); its Table S1 (peptide sequences) was not retrieved. Methods were taken from the PRIDE protocol text and the bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/141622), whose Methods text for the screen is essentially identical to the PRIDE protocol.

Peptide sequences and gene symbols of the baits are not given in any retrieved source; baits are identified by the submitters' UniProt-accession_mutation IDs verbatim. For ARHGAP36_cntrl_1/_2 the wt/mut forms are covered only by the uniform PRIDE Fw/Rev statement (no ARHGAP36 peptide entry was identified in proteinGroups); SOS1_cntrl and WIP_cntrl wt/mut entries are present in proteinGroups.

Blank runs B1-B3: PRIDE says only "B blank". They contain both light and heavy lysate proteins (proteinGroups summed Intensity L 0.9-1.0e11 and H 0.8-2.1e11 per blank run, 806-850 protein groups quantified), consistent with blank membrane spots from the light- and heavy-lysate membranes; that each channel is a separate spot from the respective membrane is inferred from the two-membrane design, not stated.

comment[precursor mass tolerance] = not available (MaxQuant 1.5.2.8 does not record it in parameters.txt; no mqpar.xml). The protocol says "Default settings were kept", but no retrieved source states the MaxQuant 1.5.2.8 default main-search tolerance, so 4.5 ppm is not asserted. Consequence: parse_sdrf convert-openms exits 1 ("Cannot read precursor mass tolerance: not available"), as in campaign precedent PXD014368.
characteristics[developmental stage] "pediatric stage" (HsapDv:0000264) is not in EFO, giving a validate-sdrf warning (not an error).

Follow-up experiments of the paper (GLUT1 BioID SILAC in HEK293, iPSC imaging) are not part of this deposit (PXD010027 is the "peptide-protein interaction screen" sub-deposit; its 264 raw files are all PepArray2 runs). reconcile's organism_part_from_cultured_material finding is triggered by the description's mention of patient-derived iPSCs, which are not samples here.
